title: Getting Started with haze

title: Getting Started with haze
text: main workhorse pervertexdata.smoothnn(), performs nearest-neighbor smoothing using kk-ring neighborhood vertex.
code: library("haze")  # Load a FreeSurfer mesh and per-vertex data mesh <- freesurferformats::read.fs.surface(   system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_mesh_lh_white", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE)) thickness <- freesurferformats::read.fs.morph(   system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_lh_thickness", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE))  # Smooth: k=2 neighborhood, 300 iterations smoothed <- pervertexdata.smoothnn(mesh, thickness, num_iter = 300L, k = 2L) #> Warning in rgl.init(initValue, onlyNULL): RGL: unable to open X11 display #> Warning: 'rgl.init' failed, will use the null device. #> See '?rgl.useNULL' for ways to avoid this warning.

text: smoothing many datasets mesh, pre-compute adjacency list mesh.adj() use pervertexdata.smoothnn.adj(): adjacency can reused: Multiple overlays (matrix, one per row) automatically smoothed parallel:

text: like pre-compute mesh neighborhood re-use smoothing many datasets mesh, use mesh.adj combination pervertexdata.smoothnn.adj instead. Help specific function can accessed usual R manner: ?<function>, replace <function> function name. Like : ?pervertexdata.smoothnn. Run example(<function>) see live demo uses function <function>. Like : example(pervertexdata.smoothnn). unit tests come package essentially list examples illustrate use functions. examples get started:
code: library("haze");  # Example 1: Smooth neuroimaging data on a human brain mesh in FreeSurfer format (see Fig.1 above): mesh = freesurferformats::read.fs.surface(system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_mesh_lh_white", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE)); per_vertex_data = freesurferformats::read.fs.morph(system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_lh_thickness", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE)); smoothed_data = pervertexdata.smoothnn(mesh, per_vertex_data, num_iter = 300L, k = 2);  # Example 2: Smooth random data on an rgl tetrahedron: mesh2 = rgl::tetrahedron3d(); pvd = rnorm(nrow(mesh2$vb), mean = 5.0, sd = 1.0); pvd_smoothed = pervertexdata.smoothnn(mesh2, pvd, num_iter = 30L);  # Example 3: Like 1, but re-use the adjacency list representation of the mesh to smooth several per-vertex data overlays on the same mesh: mesh = freesurferformats::read.fs.surface(system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_mesh_lh_white", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE)); mesh_adj = mesh.adj(mesh, k = 1L); # compute 1-ring neighborhood data1 = rnorm(length(mesh_adj), mean=1.0, sd=0.1); # generate random data data2 = rnorm(length(mesh_adj), mean=5.0, sd=0.1); # generate more random data smoothed_data1 = pervertexdata.smoothnn.adj(mesh_adj, data1, num_iter = 15L); smoothed_data2 = pervertexdata.smoothnn.adj(mesh_adj, data2, num_iter = 15L);  # Example 4: Like 3, but smooth the overlays in parallel on several CPU cores: mesh = freesurferformats::read.fs.surface(system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_mesh_lh_white", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE)); mesh_adj = mesh.adj(mesh, k = 1L); # compute 1-ring neighborhood data1 = rnorm(length(mesh_adj), mean=1.0, sd=0.1); # generate random data data2 = rnorm(length(mesh_adj), mean=5.0, sd=0.1); # generate more random data pvd = rbind(data1, data2); # Turn your data into a matrix, one overlay per row. options("mc.cores" = 2L);   # Request to run on 2 cores in parallel. smoothed_pvd = pervertexdata.smoothnn.adj(mesh_adj, pvd, num_iter = 15L); # Compute the smoothed matrix. When a matrix is passed, the rows are automatically handled in parallel, there is nothing more to do.

what: FreeSurfer: Mapping between true Gaussian smoothing and nearest neighbor smoothing
title: Smoothing of per-Vertex Data on Triangular Meshes
text: Note: haze package can used arbitrary meshes, section specific computational neuroimaging (use haze ). Ignore unless working FreeSurfer neuroimaging software suite. True Gaussian smoothing triangular mesh requires geodesic distances vertices, slow compute. FreeSurfer avoids emulating Gaussian smoothing many iterations nearest neighbor (1-ring) averaging – exactly package . trick makes valid repeated local averaging converges Gaussian kernel (central limit theorem graph): enough iterations, effective smoothing kernel approximately Gaussian, geodesic distances needed . FreeSurfer converts requested FWHM number iterations empirical formula (see MRISfwhm2niters() utils/mrisutils.cpp FreeSurfer source): avg_vertex_area mean vertex area mesh (mm^2), 7 approximates average number 1-ring neighbors vertex cortical surface, 1.14 empirical fudge factor fitted FreeSurfer measured FWHM smoothed output matches requested one. haze provides exact conversion convenience, can use FWHM values FreeSurfer picking num_iter: following table shows settings FreeSurfer uses fsaverage templates. Note based group-average surface area stored FreeSurfer template surface files (see ), differ slightly fwhm2niters(surface = ...) computes raw mesh geometry. Tbl.1: Mapping true Gaussian smoothing nearest neighbor smoothing FreeSurfer full resolution (fsaverage) meshes. FWHM, full width half maximum; gstd, Gaussian standard deviations; k, neighborhood size mesh (edge distance). table obtained running mris_surf2surf, FreeSurfer v6. : values specific mesh resolution valid specific use case computational neuroimaging. helper table differ: FreeSurfer normalizes mean vertex area group-average surface area templates (group_avg_surface_area, 82,000 mm^2 per hemisphere fsaverage), larger raw geometric area fsaverage meshes (65,000 mm^2 fsaverage lh white surface shipped package). FreeSurfer therefore reports fewer iterations fwhm2niters(surface = ...) computes raw mesh (e.g. FWHM = 10 mm: 74 iterations FreeSurfer vs. 92 raw mesh area). reproduce FreeSurfer’s exact numbers, pass FreeSurfer-equivalent mean vertex area explicitly: conversion calibrated 1-ring neighborhood (k = 1), FreeSurfer uses; fwhm2niters() niters2fwhm() issue warning pass different k.
code: gstd   = fwhm / sqrt(log(256))                     # FWHM -> Gaussian sigma (log(256) = 8*ln(2)) niters = round(1.14 * (4 * pi * gstd^2) / (7 * avg_vertex_area)) # 'What num_iter in haze corresponds to FreeSurfer's --fwhm 10?' mesh = freesurferformats::read.fs.surface(system.file("extdata", "fsaverage_mesh_lh_white", package = "haze", mustWork = TRUE)); fwhm2niters(10, surface = mesh);   # 92 iterations, approximating ~10 mm FWHM for this mesh  # Or with a pre-computed mean vertex area: fwhm2niters(10, avg_vertex_area = 0.5);  # The inverse, e.g. to report the equivalent FWHM of an iteration count: niters2fwhm(92, surface = mesh);   # ~10 mm fwhm2niters(10, avg_vertex_area = 82167 / 163842);   # 74 iterations, matching FreeSurfer

title: Convert FreeSurfer Gaussian smoothing FWHM to number of NN smoothing iterations. — fwhm2niters
text: fwhm numeric scalar, desired full width half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian smoothing kernel millimeters, used FreeSurfer's mris_fwhm --fwhm <fwhm> mri_surf2surf --fwhm <fwhm>. surface mesh, represented fs.surface instance freesurferformats package, tmesh3d instance rgl, character string representing path surface file load. Used compute mean vertex area. Ignored avg_vertex_area given. avg_vertex_area numeric scalar, mean vertex area mesh square millimeters (squared mesh units). NULL (default), computed surface. See details FreeSurfer's numbers differ. k positive integer, k-ring neighborhood size use NN smoothing. FreeSurfer-based calibration valid 1-ring neighborhood (k=1); warning issued otherwise.

title: Convert FreeSurfer Gaussian smoothing FWHM to number of NN smoothing iterations. — fwhm2niters
text: integer scalar, number NN smoothing iterations (num_iter parameter pervertexdata.smoothnn) approximates Gaussian smoothing requested FWHM.

title: Convert FreeSurfer Gaussian smoothing FWHM to number of NN smoothing iterations. — fwhm2niters
text: True Gaussian smoothing triangular mesh require computing geodesic distances (many) vertex pairs, slow. FreeSurfer avoids emulating Gaussian many iterations nearest-neighbor (1-ring) averaging: whole trick repeated local averaging converges Gaussian kernel (central limit theorem graph), geodesic distances needed . iteration cheap local operation (average vertex direct edge neighbors), exactly pervertexdata.smoothnn implements. relationship effective Gaussian standard deviation gstd n iterations mean vertex area avg_vertex_area calibrated empirically FreeSurfer MRISfwhm2niters() (see utils/mrisutils.cpp FreeSurfer source): 7 approximates average number neighbors 1-ring triangulated cortical surface, 1.14 empirical fudge factor FreeSurfer fitted measured FWHM smoothed output matches requested one. function inverse niters2fwhm. Note matching FreeSurfer's outputs: FreeSurfer normalizes mean vertex area group-average surface area stored template surface files (group_avg_surface_area, 82,000 mm^2 per hemisphere fsaverage), larger raw geometric area fsaverage meshes (65,000 mm^2 packaged fsaverage lh white surface). FreeSurfer therefore reports somewhat lower iteration counts get avg_vertex_area computed directly meshes (e.g., FWHM = 10 mm fsaverage: 74 iterations FreeSurfer vs. 92 raw mesh area). reproduce FreeSurfer's exact numbers, pass avg_vertex_area = group_avg_surface_area / nvertices (0.5015 mm^2 fsaverage templates).
code: gstd   = fwhm / sqrt(log(256))                     # FWHM -> Gaussian sigma (log(256) = 8*ln(2))   niters = round(1.14 * (4 * pi * gstd^2) / (7 * avg_vertex_area))
